developer: Contour, TerraWatt, THO Investments, Steadfast City, ARCO Construction (Armory Innovation District team)
project: Armory Innovation Data Center, 3728 Market Street

documents.title: Community Benefits Agreement term sheet (City of St. Louis). The recorded CBA with the Land Clearance for Redevelopment Authority had not been executed as of late August 2026.
Conditional use permit provisions (City summary of the nine conditions)
City page: Armory data center conditional use
STLPR: Board of Adjustment upholds permit with new rules after 11-hour hearing

community_fund.controlled_by: A fund at the City's direction, for multimodal improvements such as the Brickline Greenway, a digital access plan, and economic and environmental justice programs.
community_fund.notes: $30 per square foot of approved data center development, estimated at $15,750,000. Timing of payment is not stated. This is a term sheet commitment; the recorded agreement that would make it binding was not yet executed as of August 28, 2026.

sources.quote: $30 per square foot of approved data center development, an estimated $15,750,000

clawbacks.notes: Liquidated damages rather than incentive repayment, since no incentives were given. Revenue: $15,000 per $100,000 shortfall against projected annual tax revenue if not met by 2029. Jobs: $2,000 per job short of 25, 50, then 100 median-wage jobs, for 20 years. No trigger tied to the facility ceasing operation.

decommissioning.notes: A decommissioning plan to remove and recycle e-waste must be filed if the facility is vacant for more than a year. No bond, escrow, or letter of credit.

grid_costs.governed_by: Ameren Missouri large-load tariff approved by the Missouri Public Service Commission in November 2025 (75 MW and up; 12-year minimum term; exit fees)
grid_costs.notes: The permit requires the petitioner to fund any project-specific additional electrical infrastructure. Any minimum bill comes from the Ameren tariff, not the city deal. Reasonable efforts to reach 50 percent renewable within five years with RECs as fallback; PUE of 1.25 or better with annual reporting; generators Tier 4 and never for general power. The Board of Adjustment added an on-site renewable requirement and a ban on generator testing on bad-air days.

sources.quote: must fund any project-specific additional electrical infrastructure

water.notes: Closed-loop system with air-cooled chillers required. Written agreement with the Water Division to pay all fees and impact fees, fund a hydraulic model study, and rectify impacts on existing customers. Annual water-usage reporting, which may be made public. No volume cap.

noise.measured_at: All adjoining parcel lines, measured in an annual third-party noise report to the Health Director and Zoning Administrator. The standard is the City noise ordinance, not a number in the deal.
noise.notes: Equipment must sit in acoustically treated enclosures away from street frontages. Generator testing only on weekdays from 10 to 12 and 2 to 5. A university acoustics researcher testified that low-frequency noise cannot be absorbed at feasible wall thicknesses.

jobs.notes: Enforceable minimums of 25 median-wage jobs in year one, 50 in year two, and 100 after, for 20 years, backed by $2,000 per job in liquidated damages. First-source hiring for entry-level jobs. Prevailing wage and M/WBE compliance for the developer and contractors. Construction under a project labor agreement with the St. Louis Building Trades. Enforceability depends on the recorded CBA being executed.

local_contracting.notes: M/WBE participation, prevailing wage, and a project labor agreement. The developer builds Market Street sidewalks and a pathway to the Grand MetroLink station. No haul-route repair term.

transparency.notes: Tenant must be disclosed unless commercially unreasonable due to national security. Annual reports on electricity, waste heat, water, PUE, noise, and e-waste. The noise report is by a third party. No NDA found. The process drew criticism: aldermen were told hours before a virtual vote, and 13 appeals plus a circuit court suit followed.

tax.notes: The developer committed not to seek local tax abatement or other financial incentives and to cooperate in terminating the existing Armory TIF. The City projects $432M in taxes and fees over ten years.

sources.quote: will not seek local tax abatement or other financial incentives

criticisms.summary: The recorded community benefits agreement is still a term sheet. Until it is executed, the liquidated damages and job minimums are promises, not obligations.
Aldermen were notified hours before a virtual vote; 13 appeals were filed and a judicial-review petition followed on August 28, 2026.
Air quality and low-frequency noise concerns near a children's hospital about a quarter mile away.
